name: Pennsylvania

sales.rateNote: State rate 6%. By law a 1% local tax is added in Allegheny County (total 7%) and a 2% local tax in Philadelphia (total 8%).

local.levies: counties and the City of Philadelphia may impose a local sales, use and hotel occupancy tax; only Allegheny County (1%) and Philadelphia (2%) do
local.capNote: Local rates fixed by law: 1% Allegheny County, 2% Philadelphia. As of January 2010 only these two have imposed local tax.

groceries.note: Food that is not ready-to-eat (grocery store food) is exempt, as are candy and gum; ready-to-eat food from restaurants and caterers is taxable.

clothing.note: Most clothing is exempt regardless of price; formal day or evening apparel, fur articles, sporting clothing, accessories and ornamental wear are taxable.

otherRates.note: Same rate as sales tax, plus 1% local hotel occupancy tax where a local tax is imposed; also applies to rentals booked through online brokers.
3% Public Transportation Assistance tax on total lease payments (30+ days), on top of sales tax.
2% Vehicle Rental Tax on rentals of 29 days or less by companies with 5+ vehicles, plus a $2 per day PTA fee and sales tax.

sales.holidayNote: No sales tax holiday is listed by the Department of Revenue; most clothing, groceries and school textbooks are exempt year-round.

useTax.note: Use tax equals the sales tax rate: 6% state plus 1% for items delivered to or used in Allegheny County and 2% for Philadelphia; individuals can report it on the PA-40.

facts.text: Pennsylvania's sales tax is 6%, with a 1% local tax added by law in Allegheny County and 2% in Philadelphia.
Only Allegheny County and the City of Philadelphia impose a local sales tax; vendors located there must collect it.
Most clothing is exempt, but formal wear, bridal apparel, fur articles and sporting clothing are taxable.
Candy and gum, textbooks and residential heating fuels (oil, electricity, gas, coal, firewood) are exempt.
Digital products, including canned software and digital goods, are subject to sales and use tax.
Each new highway tire carries a $1 PTA fee, and car rentals pay $2 per day plus a 2% Vehicle Rental Tax.

property.levied: local only: counties, municipalities and school districts; values set by county assessment offices

assessment.text: Property is assessed by the county assessment office; there is no statewide reassessment cycle or single statewide assessment ratio in the Department materials read. School districts cannot raise property tax rates faster than an annual inflation index without a voter referendum (Act 1 of 2006).

homestead.name: Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion (Act 1 of 2006)
homestead.text: Reduces the taxable assessed value of a primary residence for school property taxes, funded by state gaming revenue; the amount varies by school district. In Philadelphia the state relief lowers the wage tax instead.
homestead.applyBy: Apply to the county assessment office by March 1; reapplication cannot be required more than once every three years.

otherRelief.name: Property Tax/Rent Rebate (PTRR)
otherRelief.text: Rebate of $380 to $1,000 for homeowners and renters 65+, widows and widowers 50+, and people with disabilities 18+, with household income of $48,110 or less; supplemental rebates of $190-$500 for some low-income homeowners and in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and Scranton. 2025 claims accepted until December 31, 2026.

otherRelief.name: Farmstead exclusion
otherRelief.text: Covers agricultural buildings on a farm of at least 10 contiguous acres that is the owner's primary residence; can be combined with the homestead exclusion.

facts.text: The PTRR maximum standard rebate rose to $1,000 (from $650) and the income limit is now indexed to cost of living; it is $48,110 for 2025 claims.
PTRR rebates are paid starting July 1 each year and applicants must reapply annually.
School districts must notify residential owners by December 31 each year about the homestead exclusion application.
Under Act 1, a school district must hold a voter referendum to raise taxes beyond its inflation index unless a referendum exception applies.
The state realty transfer tax is 1% of the property value on transfer, often with an additional local realty transfer tax collected by county Recorders of Deeds.
Since 1971 the PTRR program has delivered nearly $9 billion in relief, funded by gaming revenue.
